captions.tab:main37: Gray-128 campaign over 37 category-benchmarks: macro image/pixel AUROC, retention of image AUROC at 60\% training data, and Spearman agreement between the anomaly map and the physics residual on defective images.
captions.tab:mvteccats: Per-category results, gray-128 campaign (MVTec AD); pixel AUROC for all three methods.
captions.tab:visaloco: Per-category image AUROC (gray-128): VisA and MVTec LOCO.
captions.tab:h2data: Network-fitting data retention on CONSTRUCT (gray-128): performance under 40\% and 60\% network-fitting reduction; the prior stays calibrated from the full defect-free directory.
captions.tab:seedrob: Seed robustness on the primary benchmarks (seeds 42/0/1/2, gray-128).
captions.tab:h3ab: Physics-channel attribution on CONSTRUCT: zeroing the fixed input channel at test time.
captions.tab:plugin: Feature-level plug-in: PatchCore-lite with per-patch equilibrium statistics appended to the descriptors (image AUROC; fit-data retention in last columns).
captions.tab:rgbfull: RGB/256, 24-epoch schedule, mean$\pm$std over seeds 42/0/1 (image AUROC; pixel AUROC columns; PGDN wins 10/45 category-seed pairs).
captions.tab:rgbextras: RGB/256 manipulations (image AUROC, 24-epoch). Source rows: fractal$\to$external anomaly source; colour rows: luminance prior$\to$colour-aware prior; data rows: 100\%$\to$60\% training data.
captions.tab:budget: Published-budget arms (700 epochs, seed 42): under the longer schedule the data-driven twin degrades while the physics arm holds or improves; the cause of the twin's degradation is not established here.
captions.tab:router: Label-free routing versus the constant-choice baseline and the oracle. Regret is the mean per-decision AUROC loss relative to always choosing \draem{} (negative = gain); no label-free router attains negative regret.
captions.tab:pro: MVTec LOCO AUPRO@0.3 computed with the conventional PRO metric on our tested subset and split (not the dataset authors' official AU-sPRO protocol); overall / structural / logical.
captions.tab:sota: Published state of the art 2021--2025 (MVTec AD means; venues per the primary publication records; reference context, not capacity-matched: RGB 224--256$^2$). All methods use large-scale pretrained backbones except DRAEM, whose networks are trained from scratch (lr $10^{-4}$, MultiStepLR, DTD anomaly source); CLIP-based methods (WinCLIP) use web-scale vision--language pretraining rather than ImageNet classification. PGDN entries are 15-category macro means; the twin's macro pixel AUROC is given in the last column for the same aggregation.
captions.tab:factorialpc: Per-category factorial results (image AUROC, seed 42): a macro average conceals opposite per-category effects, so both are shown; the real-category macro excludes the synthetic CONSTRUCT unit.
captions.tab:interaction: Channel$\times$coupling interaction with the reconstruction loss disabled (difference-in-differences of macro image AUROC over the five factorial categories, percentage points; negative = antagonism). Replicated across seeds; SD is the population convention across seeds. Real-only sensitivity rows recompute the contrast on real defects (macro3: screw/capsule/bottle from the released per-image scores; macro4 adds cashew from the standard factorial evaluations recorded in the interaction record): negative at every seed, so the additive antagonism is not an artifact of the synthetic unit's limited metric headroom (on CONSTRUCT the input arm saturates at $1.000$ and coupling reaches $0.996$).
captions.tab:smoothfact: Smooth-defect test across all eight factorial configurations (frozen checkpoints, seed-42 training, paired generators over up to 30 held-out normal images (30/23/20 for screw/capsule/bottle), fixed seed): the drop appears with the coupling loss (screw $-26.4$ coupling-only) and is absent from baseline, input-only, and reconstruction-only arms -- component-level isolation of a category-dependent failure family.
captions.tab:smoothfactrep: Smooth-minus-Perlin difference (pp) of Table~\ref{tab:smoothfact} replicated across training seeds 42/0/1 (frozen checkpoints, paired-background protocol, up-to-30 backgrounds): the screw coupling failure appears in every seed; the capsule and bottle input$+$coupling failures appear in two of three seeds.
captions.tab:gradprobe: Coupling-gradient conflict probe on trained checkpoints: fraction of the segmentation-gradient mass on defect-mask pixels where the coupling term pushes the opposite direction ($|g_{\mathrm{seg}}|$-weighted), and the mean sign of the coupling gradient on mask pixels (positive $=$ suppression, per $\partial C/\partial p_j=(\bar z_p - z_j)/P$).
captions.tab:gradparam: Parameter-level gradient conflict on trained checkpoints: norm ratio $\|g_C^{\lambda}\|/\|g_{\mathrm{seg}}\|$ with $g_C^{\lambda}=\nabla_{\theta}(\lambda_C C)$ the already loss-weighted coupling gradient, and cosine alignment over the shared parameters (mean over two batches of eight images). On screw the coupling gradient is strongly anti-aligned with the segmentation gradient (cosine $-0.6$ to $-0.97$) and can dominate it in norm (ratio up to $10.8$), while the non-failing coupling-only arms of capsule and bottle remain aligned on Perlin defects.
captions.tab:defectsweep: Defect-family dose-response on screw: the smooth-defect generator's contrast, defect frequency, and binary mask smoothing varied one factor at a time over the same 30 paired backgrounds (frozen seed-42 factorial checkpoints). The deriv.\ ratio is the gradient energy inside the defect mask relative to the clean background. The coupling-only arm improves substantially only at the highest contrast ($0.484\to0.849$); the input$+$coupling and full arms remain at chance across the whole family; the uncoupled arms are not uniformly robust (reconstruction-only loses $23.6$ pp at the lowest contrast; input-only loses $19.0$ pp from mid to low (coarser) defect frequency).
captions.tab:lamc: Coupling-weight intervention on the screw coupling-only arm (8-epoch gray recipe, 30 paired backgrounds, fixed evaluation seed). Seed 42: CUDA-trained weights with the CPU-trained factorial baseline reused as C-off. Seed 0: fully matched CUDA controls including C-off. The smooth-defect failure onsets between $\lambda_C=0.1$ and $0.25$ at both seeds, and the over-weighted term degrades the Perlin score at $0.5$--$1.0$; absolute deterioration accompanies the family gap. The sweep supports deterioration between the sampled weights in this setting, not a universal critical threshold.
captions.tab:compatv2: Compatibility v2: edge density uses a pooled 95th-percentile threshold across categories (informative; varies 0.000--0.152). Held-out rule correctness versus the constant-choice baseline, compared with exact McNemar on discordant pairs ($p_M$; thresholds fitted on development categories only); the diagnostic column reports a two-sided binomial test against chance ($p_{\mathrm{bin}}$). No descriptor reliably beats its constant-choice baseline; reverse-split edge density is 5/7 versus 4/7, a numerical edge without statistical support.
captions.tab:factorial: Factorial ablation of the three interventions (input channel / derivative reconstruction loss / coupling loss), gray-128, five boundary categories (screw, bottle, capsule, cashew, CONSTRUCT), seed 42; SD is across those five category units (including the synthetic CONSTRUCT unit), not across training seeds.
captions.tab:controls: Channel-content controls: the full prior map replaced by simpler derivative descriptors or a distribution-preserving shuffle (image AUROC; full-\(z\) column shows img/pix).
captions.tab:official: Reference-style recipe audit (lr $10^{-4}$, MultiStepLR, 700 epochs, external source), including the audit extension to the remaining below-chance categories (toothbrush, leather). A decomposition arm on screw (scheduled lr, original fractal source) gives twin $0.669$ / PGDN $0.923$.
captions.tab:ksdd2pixel: KolektorSDD2 localization from the canonical paired evaluation (official GT masks; 1004 test images, 110 anomalous; identical seeded pixel indices for both arms --- 4096 per image at gray-128, 4.11M pooled, and 16384 at RGB-256, 16.45M pooled; AP uses the recall-increment convention of scikit-learn). PGDN-minus-twin pixel-AUROC difference, 95\% image-cluster bootstrap CIs: $[-0.066,+0.064]$ at gray-128 (includes zero: a difference is not established, which is not equivalence) and $[+0.108,+0.275]$ at RGB-256, conditional on the tested checkpoints and protocol; pixel AP descriptively favours PGDN at both operating points, and both arms deteriorate absolutely at RGB-256.
captions.tab:realbridge: Real MVTec defects split at the median of the prior's own mean response $z$ inside the ground-truth mask (independent of detector outcomes); image AUROC per group with all defect-free test images as negatives (seed-42 factorial arms). The synthetic coupling failure does not predict real harm on screw, where the coupling-only arm is best on both groups; bottle shows a real coupling cost on both groups.
captions.tab:realmod: Matched coupling moderation on real defects: $M=E_{\mathrm{weak}}-E_{\mathrm{strong}}$, where $E_g$ is the change in group AUROC when coupling is enabled (reconstruction off; groups fixed at the seed-42 $z$ median; shared normal negatives). Nominal exploratory 95\% percentile CIs from the released paired image-cluster bootstrap (10{,}000 replicates, pooled multinomial image resampling, groups fixed; moderation\_bootstrap.py). All eighteen point estimates are negative; only bottle's input-enabled intervals exclude zero in every seed --- screw and capsule remain directional observations whose intervals include zero.
captions.tab:smooth: Weak-derivative defect test: image AUROC of both arms on matched standard (Perlin) versus smooth low-contrast synthetic defects over the same defect-free images.
